record.title: Myanmar closes Second Friendship Bridge cargo route
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Second Mae Sot Myawaddy Friendship Bridge
record.crossings: Second Mae Sot Myawaddy Friendship Bridge
record.direction: Cargo across the Myanmar side of the bilateral bridge; closure affected trade in both directions. Initial May 28 reopening observation specifically confirms Myanmar-side truck traffic.
record.enforcement: Limited truck activity observed by traders at reopening.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence; present status not inferred
record.official_rationale: Conflict cited by local reporting; Thai official discussions also address Myanmar import regulations.
record.uncertainty: Cargo resumed at low levels; not complete return to normal. NationThailand repeats ElevenMyanmar, so not a third independent source.

historical.duration_note: Calendar-date difference to the stated partial reopening for the specified category and crossing; not exact hours or universal closure

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Thai MFA confirms Myanmar-announced Bridge II closure; Eleven reports actual limited resumed traffic.
August 18, 2025 is explicit in both accounts.
May 28, 2026 morning truck operation is reported, initially specifically from Myanmar.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The recorded rationale and claim assessment support the selected subcategories. All applicable broad categories are retained together; no primary rationale is imposed. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Eleven attributes closure to military conflict; MFA discusses import regulations without establishing a separate protectionist cause.
Cargo Bridge II is distinct from passenger Bridge I. Full two-way normal operation is not demonstrated.
A 283-day calendar difference is retained only to initial partial cargo resumption; the source describes the route closure throughout this spell.

record.rationale_phase_note: One current coded subtype; no assertion that all possible motives have been identified.

followup_reviews.Research finding: The primary MFA account explicitly dates closure to 18 August 2025. Eleven describes limited morning Myanmar-side traffic; Khaosod reports a Thai truck entering Myawaddy after midday; DVB describes agricultural cargo entering Thailand and licence hurdles. These support the existing qualified first-cargo endpoint on 28 May and its 283-day calendar difference, without full normalization.
followup_reviews.Challenge verdict: Accepted within the root decision; see frozen challenge

followup_reviews.Root decision: Accept three scoped additions, six phase additions, two targeted findings and two EA001 summary refinements. Preserve held Myawaddy timings, qualified first-cargo Teknaf endpoint, formal-only Singkhon permissions, separate humanitarian exceptions, source dependence and unlocated geometry.
followup_reviews.Issue dispositions: REC50-R28-Q02 — The endpoint is initial partial cargo resumption. This narrow review does not newly reconstruct every intervening day, verify every commodity or convert related/reprinted reports into independent origins.
